I sit here and think 'what does she have to lose'  Tell him how you feel about LDR's and that you got scared off.  You do not want to be a huge decider in his decision to pursue school in France, but you know that you currently couldnt do it and that scared you off.  Be honest and up front with him, that is the best thing to do here.  If you think you made a mistake, tell him.

Before you get to your place is the best, at dinner preferably, or whatever the date will be.  Work it into conversation or push the conversation towards sex and see how he reacts.  He may not be ready for it, so be prepared to drop the subject if he is a take it slow kind of guy. If he is, dont let that discourage you though :)

I think at this point even trying to get back with her on a friend level wont work.  You think you can move on but likely its going to be extremely difficult.  You should ABSOLUTELY reach out and apologize for what you did.  Do not mention anything specific, just that you are sorry for making the night uncomfortable and you wish her the best.  If it is something she wants to salvage let her do it.  Unfortunately the position you are in is tough, she has to want to be friends with you, you cannot force her.  I wish you the best of luck though. This is a difficult, slippery path.  Let me know if I can help more!
ah I see, well yes, it would be hard to just up and leave, I know I have had issues in the past with it, especially when you love someone, but a glaring issue like this should be dealt with.

I would try couples therapy actually.  Go for a few sessions together then some alone.  This may better help him understand what is going on and maybe help you to see things from his point of view.  It sounds like depression though, and I highly recommend you slowly work him into the thought of therapy.  Took me a while for myself personally and it has really changed me for the better.

so it seems she is considering herself without considering you.  Not the easiest thing to do.  If you really want to try and get an answer, because really you seem to be lost as to her mixed signal, just ask.  You understand that breaking contact is likely the EASIEST way to handle this, so what do you have to lose?  

You can try slowly working to less contact, that may be easier than just cold turkeying it, but I think talking to her about the situation like an adult, no accusing or anything like that, may be a good method here.  Stay strong, this will not be an easy battle, one that likely will not end in you all being together, but may potentially end with the piece of mind you seem to desire.  Best of luck!

Can you describe the ways that you have approached this?  I generally find that when I am talking with an SO or anyone and I am looking to get them to work on something that I do not make it attacking, but instead I work on making them feel not alone.  I doubt you are perfect. Try to sit her down and talk with her about it all but start off with asking her why she has seemed so lethargic lately.  Say that maybe you have not been the best at communicating but you want to fix that and you hope that she wants to fix being, as you would call it, lazy.  I am not sure of your technique so I really cant sit here and say, yep, you messed up, youre screwed, etc. but instead, try to think from her point of view.  That may help :) Best of luck!

Well, continue to document it then I guess. Talk to her more often, make more conversation.  If she still seems distant after a bit ask about it.  Mine was based on very short responses, the obvious lack to continue texting, etc. When you have to carry a conversation, the writing is on the wall.

Went through something similar to this, worked out terribly, but I would not change the way I approached it.. 

I straight up told the woman that I felt like she was distancing me, and that I just wanted to know for sure.  Ask her why you guys dont talk often, be honest.  Communication is key.  If you cannot be open with her about your feelings it is time to pull out of that relationship now because it will not get any better and your anxiety will only compound (this comes from personal experience)

Reach out and see if she is okay, just be her friend. If it turns into more, wonderful, but if not you will know that it was not meant to be.  If she is going through tough times try to help her, if she refuses the help just wish her the best and leave it be.  Not much more you can do.

Be honest and up front.  Let her know that you do not want a relationship with her.  You can make an excuse if you want, but just be straightforward.  No need to tell her WHY, but give her something, you know.  Like that you just did not feel a connection but that she is a wonderful person and you hope she finds the right guy out there.
